Using 40 fMRI datasets, researchers determined that these methods do not measure the same underlying process, indicating that current tools fail to effectively capture the capacity for emotional regulation.

Why it matters

The findings challenge the validity of current methods used to assess emotional resilience, a core component of cognitive behavioral therapy, and call for a fundamental reassessment of how reappraisal capacity is measured and interpreted.

Global · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 04 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

A study in Science found that Manx shearwaters experience jet lag when flying across time zones, causing their internal clocks to desynchronize with local time. This desynchronization skews their sun-based compass, leading to measurable navigational deviations of up to 15 degrees during homing flights. The findings were derived from GPS data of 3,688 foraging trips by 1,045 birds, though the study notes it is not a controlled experiment and cannot confirm other jet lag symptoms.

Why it matters

The research provides insights into bio-inspired autonomous navigation systems and suggests that studying animals that routinely experience jet lag may offer strategies to mitigate jet lag effects in humans.

'Pretty strong correlation' between enrolment changes and lower enrolment rate - electoral law expert

NZ · Notable · Updated

Briefing produced 01 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

New Zealand's provisional voter enrolment rate for the 2026 election is 93.6%, down from 94.7% in 2023, following a law change that prohibited enrolment on election day and during the advanced voting period.
